name: Sisera
overview: Sisera was a male military leader known as the commander of Jabin's army, a position that highlights his significant role in the conflict described in the Book of Judges. He lived in Harosheth-hagoyim and served as the captain of the army of Hazor, indicating his leadership over a powerful Canaanite force. His military command situates him as a notable antagonist in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Sisera appears as a proper name in the Scriptures without a given meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as Sisera, with no additional titles or meanings provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Sisera's relationship as the army commander under King Jabin, indicating a military hierarchy. He is also connected to Jael, who is identified as his victim, marking a pivotal personal encounter in the narrative. Beyond these, no family relationships are detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Sisera's significance lies in his role as the chief military opponent of Israel during the time of the Judges. As commander of Jabin's army and captain of Hazor's forces, he represents the oppressive power against which Israel struggled. His defeat and death, particularly through the actions involving Jael, underscore God's deliverance of His people and the triumph of faith over formidable enemies.
